questions.question: Do visibly bounded fields occupy more than half the patch?
questions.definition: Count open parcels distinguished by boundaries, texture or colour, excluding woodland, water and built surfaces, and answer yes when their combined interiors exceed half the image.

questions.question: Are at least three neighbouring fields predominantly rectangular?
questions.definition: Count adjoining open parcels with four approximately straight sides and roughly right-angled corners, allowing minor boundary irregularities.

questions.question: Does one uninterrupted field occupy at least a quarter of the patch?
questions.definition: Answer yes when a single open parcel covers at least one quarter of the image without a visible road, woody strip or contrasting parcel dividing it.

questions.question: Are markedly different field sizes present together?
questions.definition: Require two substantially visible fields whose apparent areas differ by at least a factor of four, ignoring parcels mostly outside the image.

questions.question: Are there several long, narrow fields?
questions.definition: Require at least three distinct open parcels whose visible lengths are at least three times their widths.

questions.question: Does a field have a substantially curved boundary?
questions.definition: Require a field edge that visibly bends over at least 100 metres, excluding small corner rounding and pixel-scale irregularities.

questions.question: Do several fields share a common orientation?
questions.definition: Answer yes when at least three elongated fields have long axes aligned within approximately 20 degrees of one another.

questions.question: Are two differently oriented groups of fields visible?
questions.definition: Require two groups containing at least two fields each, with their dominant boundary directions differing by roughly 30 degrees or more.

questions.question: Are neighbouring fields separated by a visible vegetation strip?
questions.definition: Require a continuous red-toned strip in false colour along at least 100 metres of a shared field boundary, rather than a colour difference between field interiors.

questions.question: Does a strongly vegetated field directly adjoin a bare-looking field?
questions.definition: Require a shared boundary between a red-dominant field in false colour and a brown or grey field lacking a comparable vegetation signal.

questions.question: Do neighbouring fields show at least three distinct cover appearances?
questions.definition: Require three parcels with clearly different combinations of colour and texture, such as strong vegetation, pale vegetation and exposed-looking ground, excluding illumination differences.

questions.question: Are repeated parallel bands visible within a field?
questions.definition: Require at least three alternating bands that are individually resolvable and remain inside the same field, excluding image-wide striping.

questions.question: Does a road or track run alongside several fields?
questions.definition: Require a continuous transport-like strip bordering at least three distinct open parcels along a combined length of at least 200 metres.

questions.question: Does open agricultural-looking ground contain scattered woody clumps?
questions.definition: Require at least three separated, coarse-textured vegetation clumps within or between fields, excluding vegetation confined to one continuous woodland edge.

questions.question: Is a field bordered by woody vegetation on at least two sides?
questions.definition: Require coarse-textured vegetation to follow two distinct sides of an open parcel for at least half the visible length of each side.

questions.question: Is a woody vegetation island enclosed by open ground?
questions.definition: Require a coarse-textured vegetation block at least 30 metres across with a visible ring of open ground separating it from other woody cover.

questions.question: Do several field boundaries converge near a road junction?
questions.definition: Require at least three parcel edges to terminate within approximately 50 metres of a visible junction between road-like strips.

questions.question: Does a field combine a straight edge with an irregular opposite edge?
questions.definition: Require an open parcel with one boundary straight for at least 100 metres and an opposing boundary showing a clear curve, indentation or protrusion.

questions.question: Do narrow fields occur beside a much broader field?
questions.definition: Require at least two elongated parcels adjoining or lying within 50 metres of a parcel at least three times as wide.

questions.question: Is there a large field with a visually uniform interior?
questions.definition: Require a parcel covering at least 10 percent of the patch whose interior lacks conspicuous colour patches, bands or woody inclusions.

questions.question: Does an apparently continuous open parcel contain a sharp internal colour division?
questions.definition: Require two substantial colour zones separated by a clear line without a visible road, hedge or other physical divider.

questions.question: Do several fields meet without visible woody boundary strips?
questions.definition: Require at least three neighbouring parcels distinguished by colour or texture whose shared boundaries lack resolvable coarse-textured vegetation.

questions.question: Do adjoining vegetated fields differ strongly in false-colour redness?
questions.definition: Require two fields sharing an edge whose interiors both show vegetation but differ conspicuously in red intensity across most of their areas.

questions.question: Is there a visibly tapering field?
questions.definition: Require an open parcel whose width decreases by at least half along its visible length, excluding apparent narrowing caused solely by the image boundary.

questions.question: Are angular fields interspersed with irregular open vegetation patches?
questions.definition: Require both clearly straight-edged parcels and irregularly bounded open vegetation areas, each occupying at least 5 percent of the patch.

questions.question: Are built-looking surfaces concentrated in one compact cluster?
questions.definition: Answer yes when most visible roofs and associated hard surfaces form one cluster, with gaps between its main components generally below 50 metres.

questions.question: Are built-looking groups separated by substantial open land?
questions.definition: Require at least two groups of roof-like shapes separated by at least 100 metres of fields or other vegetation.

questions.question: Do buildings form a ribbon along a road?
questions.definition: Require repeated roof-like elements extending along at least 200 metres of a road, with the occupied ribbon clearly longer than it is wide.

questions.question: Is a small building group surrounded mainly by open ground?
questions.definition: Require a distinguishable group of roof-like shapes with fields or open vegetation around at least three quarters of its visible perimeter.

questions.question: Does a built-up edge directly face fields?
questions.definition: Require a roof-and-street cluster to share at least 100 metres of boundary with recognizable field parcels, allowing a separating road.

questions.question: Are conspicuous vegetation patches embedded among buildings?
questions.definition: Require at least two vegetated areas approximately 30 metres across within a broader arrangement of visible roofs and streets.

questions.question: Does a road cross most of the patch?
questions.definition: Require a traceable road-like corridor connecting opposite image edges or extending continuously for at least 900 metres.

questions.question: Is a road junction visible within open land?
questions.definition: Require at least three connected road arms meeting away from a dense building cluster, with fields or vegetation occupying most surrounding ground.

questions.question: Does a road make a pronounced bend?
questions.definition: Require a traceable road segment whose direction changes by at least approximately 45 degrees within the patch, excluding junction turns.

questions.question: Are two transport corridors visibly different in width?
questions.definition: Require two road-like strips each traceable for at least 150 metres, with one appearing at least twice as wide as the other.

questions.question: Does a road visibly divide a large vegetation area?
questions.definition: Require a continuous road-like strip to pass through a vegetation block with substantial vegetation extending at least 50 metres on both sides.

questions.question: Are buildings distributed along branching roads?
questions.definition: Require roof-like elements beside at least three connected road arms rather than solely along one unbranched corridor.

questions.question: Does built cover become visibly sparser toward an adjoining open area?
questions.definition: Require a transition from closely spaced roof-like elements to separated building groups and then open ground within the image.

questions.question: Are unusually large roof-like surfaces mixed with smaller roofs?
questions.definition: Require at least one coherent rectangular roof-like feature approximately 40 metres across alongside several visibly smaller roof-like features.

questions.question: Is a broad hard-looking surface attached to a building group?
questions.definition: Require a smooth grey, pale or bluish area at least 30 metres across adjoining roof-like shapes and connected to a visible access route.

questions.question: Does a built-looking cluster have an irregular, indented edge?
questions.definition: Require at least two open or vegetated indentations penetrating approximately 50 metres into the outer boundary of a building cluster.

questions.question: Do visible roads form enclosed blocks?
questions.definition: Require at least two areas enclosed by connected road-like strips, excluding field boundaries without a discernible transport surface.

questions.question: Does a road follow a woodland edge?
questions.definition: Require a road-like strip to remain within approximately 30 metres of a coarse-textured woody vegetation boundary for at least 150 metres.

questions.question: Does a road pass between contrasting land-cover patterns?
questions.definition: Require at least 150 metres of road with consistently different surroundings on its two sides, such as woodland versus fields or buildings versus open vegetation.

questions.question: Are narrow access routes visible inside a field mosaic?
questions.definition: Require at least two road- or track-like strips extending into or between recognizable fields, each traceable for approximately 100 metres.

questions.question: Does woody vegetation closely border a building group?
questions.definition: Require coarse-textured vegetation within approximately 30 metres of roof-like elements along a combined frontage of at least 100 metres.

questions.question: Is built-looking cover largely confined to one side of the patch?
questions.definition: Require identifiable buildings, with at least four fifths of their visible footprint lying within one image half and the opposite half mainly open or vegetated.

questions.question: Do buildings and vegetation form a fine-grained mosaic?
questions.definition: Require repeated alternation between roof-like surfaces and vegetation at spacings of roughly 20–100 metres across an area at least 200 metres wide.

questions.question: Are straight transport segments prominent in the landscape?
questions.definition: Require at least two road-like segments each approximately 200 metres long whose paths deviate little from a straight line.

questions.question: Does a road connect separate building groups across open land?
questions.definition: Require a traceable road joining two distinguishable roof clusters with at least 100 metres of fields or vegetation between them.

questions.question: Does open vegetation appear more intensely red than nearby woody vegetation?
questions.definition: Require a smooth-textured open vegetation area to be conspicuously brighter red in false colour than an adjacent coarse-textured woody area outside shadow.

questions.question: Does woody vegetation appear more intensely red than nearby open vegetation?
questions.definition: Require a coarse-textured woody area to be conspicuously brighter red in false colour than an adjacent smooth-textured vegetated area outside shadow.

questions.question: Are strongly red and weakly red vegetation patches intermingled?
questions.definition: Require at least three alternations between conspicuously different vegetation redness levels within a connected area, excluding obvious shadows.

questions.question: Does a vegetation area contain pale or brown-looking gaps?
questions.definition: Require at least two internal gaps approximately 20 metres across that are pale or brown in true colour and show weaker vegetation redness than their surroundings.

questions.question: Does a field have a greener-looking margin than interior?
questions.definition: Require a boundary strip at least approximately 20 metres wide to appear greener in true colour and redder in false colour than most of the field interior.

questions.question: Does a field have a greener-looking interior than margin?
questions.definition: Require a substantial field interior to appear greener in true colour and redder in false colour than a visible peripheral strip along at least two sides.

questions.question: Are diffuse vegetation-colour gradients visible within open ground?
questions.definition: Require a gradual colour transition extending over at least 50 metres inside one open area, rather than a sharp parcel boundary or cast shadow.

questions.question: Are sharply bounded vegetation-colour patches visible within a field?
questions.definition: Require at least two internal zones approximately 30 metres across separated by an abrupt change in vegetation redness without a visible physical boundary.

questions.question: Do neighbouring woody vegetation blocks have contrasting canopy appearances?
questions.definition: Require adjoining coarse-textured vegetation blocks with a consistent difference in true-colour tone or false-colour redness across areas at least 50 metres wide.

questions.question: Does a woody area have a visibly mottled canopy?
questions.definition: Require repeated light and dark or differently red canopy patches at scales of roughly 20–60 metres across a woody area at least 150 metres wide.

questions.question: Is there a woody area with a comparatively uniform canopy appearance?
questions.definition: Require a coarse-textured vegetation block at least 200 metres across with broadly consistent colour and no large internal gaps or contrasting compartments.

questions.question: Does vegetation form repeated rows or broad aligned bands?
questions.definition: Require at least three resolvable, approximately parallel vegetation bands separated by less vegetated-looking ground, without identifying a crop or planting purpose.

questions.question: Does woody cover appear open enough for background ground to show through?
questions.definition: Require repeated pale or brown spaces between coarse vegetation clumps across a substantial area, rather than a closed canopy with isolated clearings.

questions.question: Are lush-looking and dry-looking open vegetation areas present together?
questions.definition: Require both green, strongly red open vegetation and yellow-brown open cover with a weaker but discernible vegetation signal, each covering at least 5 percent of the patch.

questions.question: Does yellow or brown vegetation retain a visible false-colour vegetation signal?
questions.definition: Require a non-shadowed area at least 50 metres across that looks yellow or brown in true colour but remains visibly reddish in false colour.

questions.question: Do some vegetation patches stand out much more clearly in false colour?
questions.definition: Require at least two patches approximately 30 metres across that blend with surrounding ground in true colour but become clearly differentiated by redness in false colour.

questions.question: Does a pale field contain scattered greener-looking patches?
questions.definition: Require at least three internal patches with stronger vegetation redness inside a predominantly pale or brown field, excluding woody islands.

questions.question: Does a predominantly green field contain substantial weak-vegetation patches?
questions.definition: Require non-shadowed internal patches with conspicuously reduced false-colour redness to occupy at least approximately one tenth of an otherwise green field.

questions.question: Do vegetation-colour patterns cross visible parcel boundaries?
questions.definition: Require a similarly shaped colour anomaly or gradient to continue across at least one clear field boundary without simply following that boundary.

questions.question: Do vegetation-colour changes closely follow parcel boundaries?
questions.definition: Require at least three adjacent fields with relatively consistent internal colour and abrupt vegetation-colour differences at their shared boundaries.

questions.question: Are narrow vegetation strips redder than the larger areas they separate?
questions.definition: Require at least 100 metres of boundary vegetation that is conspicuously redder in false colour than open land on both sides.

questions.question: Does woody vegetation have a paler, less red outer margin?
questions.definition: Require a coherent edge zone approximately 20 metres wide that is lighter in true colour and less red in false colour than the adjacent canopy interior, excluding shadows.

questions.question: Does one open parcel contain both exposed-looking ground and vegetation?
questions.definition: Require soil-like brown or grey cover and visibly red vegetation each to occupy at least one quarter of the same parcel.

questions.question: Are green-looking open areas present among predominantly muted woody cover?
questions.definition: Require strongly vegetated smooth-textured openings alongside coarse-textured woody cover whose false-colour redness is consistently weaker, without inferring a season.

questions.question: Is the strongest vegetation signal concentrated in woody strips or blocks?
questions.definition: Answer yes when the conspicuously reddest substantial areas in false colour are coarse-textured woody features and the surrounding open ground is markedly less red.

questions.question: Do two contrasting cover types divide the patch into broad zones?
questions.definition: Require two visually distinct cover patterns each occupying at least one quarter of the patch and mainly lying on opposite sides of one dominant boundary.

questions.question: Does the patch contain a fine-grained mixture of cover types?
questions.definition: Require at least three visibly different cover patterns repeatedly interspersed in units mostly below approximately 100 metres across.

questions.question: Is most woody vegetation concentrated in one continuous block?
questions.definition: Require woody vegetation covering at least 10 percent of the patch, with at least four fifths of that cover belonging to one visibly connected block.

questions.question: Is woody vegetation split among several separate blocks?
questions.definition: Require at least three coarse-textured vegetation blocks approximately 30 metres across, separated by resolvable strips of open ground, water or built surfaces.

questions.question: Do narrow vegetation links connect broader vegetation blocks?
questions.definition: Require a visible vegetated corridor at least 50 metres long and clearly narrower than the two blocks it joins.

questions.question: Are two woody blocks separated by only a narrow open gap?
questions.definition: Require coarse-textured vegetation blocks facing each other across approximately 20–60 metres of non-woody ground for at least 50 metres.

questions.question: Does a woody boundary have several deep indentations?
questions.definition: Require at least two open-ground indentations extending approximately 50 metres into a coarse-textured vegetation block.

questions.question: Does woody vegetation project into open land as a narrow tongue?
questions.definition: Require a connected woody extension at least twice as long as it is wide, with open land along both sides and around its visible tip.

questions.question: Does open ground form a clearing enclosed by woody vegetation?
questions.definition: Require an open area at least 30 metres across with coarse-textured vegetation visibly surrounding its entire perimeter.

questions.question: Does open land penetrate a woody area as a broad corridor?
questions.definition: Require a non-woody strip at least 40 metres wide extending approximately 150 metres into or through a woody block.

questions.question: Are long straight edges prominent between major cover areas?
questions.definition: Require at least two boundaries between visibly contrasting cover areas that remain approximately straight for 200 metres or more.

questions.question: Are curved boundaries prominent between major cover areas?
questions.definition: Require at least two substantial cover boundaries that each change direction smoothly over a length of approximately 150 metres or more.

questions.question: Do linear vegetation features form a branching network?
questions.definition: Require connected vegetation strips with at least two visible branch junctions, excluding broad canopy areas whose internal gaps merely suggest lines.

questions.question: Do several linear features run approximately parallel across the patch?
questions.definition: Require at least three roads, vegetation strips or parcel boundaries each approximately 150 metres long and aligned within roughly 20 degrees.

questions.question: Does a diagonal corridor structure much of the patch?
questions.definition: Require a continuous road, water or vegetation corridor at least 600 metres long whose overall direction lies clearly oblique to both image axes.

questions.question: Is an extensive open area nearly surrounded by contrasting cover?
questions.definition: Require an open area at least 100 metres across with woodland, buildings or water bordering at least three quarters of its visible perimeter.

questions.question: Do three distinct cover patterns meet at one visible junction?
questions.definition: Require three substantial areas, such as woody vegetation, fields and buildings, to approach within approximately 30 metres of the same point.

questions.question: Does cover become progressively more fragmented across the patch?
questions.definition: Require one side to contain a broad continuous cover area and the opposite side to contain several separated remnants of the same visible cover pattern.

questions.question: Are small contrasting patches embedded in a dominant cover?
questions.definition: Require one cover pattern to occupy more than half the patch and contain at least three distinguishable inclusions approximately 20 metres across.

questions.question: Does one continuous vegetation area connect opposite image edges?
questions.definition: Require a visibly vegetated connection between opposite borders that remains at least approximately 30 metres wide throughout and covers less than the entire patch.

questions.question: Is woody vegetation concentrated near the image perimeter?
questions.definition: Require woody cover to occur mainly within approximately 150 metres of the image edges while the central 600-metre square is predominantly non-woody.

questions.question: Is woody vegetation concentrated around the centre of the patch?
questions.definition: Require a central woody block with most of the outer 150-metre image margin occupied by open ground, water or built surfaces.

questions.question: Do broad open and woody areas alternate across the image?
questions.definition: Require a traverse across the patch to encounter at least four alternating open and woody zones, each approximately 50 metres wide or more.

questions.question: Does a boundary separate coarse-textured vegetation from smooth vegetation?
questions.definition: Require at least 150 metres of shared edge between a woody-looking canopy texture and a comparatively smooth vegetated surface.

questions.question: Are several cover patches visibly elongated in the same direction?
questions.definition: Require at least three separate vegetation, bare-ground or built-looking patches with length-to-width ratios above two and similarly aligned long axes.

questions.question: Does open water form an elongated feature?
questions.definition: Require a smooth, non-red water-like surface with coherent banks whose visible length is at least three times its width, excluding road surfaces and cast shadows.

questions.question: Does an open-water area have a visibly irregular edge?
questions.definition: Require a confidently recognizable water surface with at least two shoreline bends or indentations larger than approximately 20 metres.

questions.question: Does visible water directly border vegetation?
questions.definition: Require a coherent water-like surface to share at least 100 metres of visible edge with red-toned vegetation, allowing a narrow unresolved bank.

questions.question: Does a visible water feature continue beyond the image boundary?
questions.definition: Require an identifiable water surface at least approximately 20 metres wide to meet an image edge with its banks or shoreline visibly continuing out of view.

questions.question: Does water create a clear break between terrestrial areas?
questions.definition: Require a continuous water-like strip at least approximately 20 metres wide with visible land on both sides over a length of at least 100 metres.

questions.question: Does open water contrast strongly with nearby red-toned vegetation?
questions.definition: Require a coherent water-like area at least 30 metres across that is dark or non-red in false colour beside conspicuously red vegetation.

questions.question: Is there a sinuous vegetation corridor through open land?
questions.definition: Require a red-toned strip approximately 20–100 metres wide that bends repeatedly over at least 200 metres, whether or not water is visible.

questions.question: Does greener-looking vegetation follow a narrow dark corridor?
questions.definition: Require stronger vegetation redness along at least 100 metres of a dark linear feature than in the adjoining open ground, without assuming the feature contains water.

questions.question: Do narrow dark channels or ditches subdivide open ground?
questions.definition: Require at least two connected or parallel dark strips traceable for approximately 100 metres whose form suggests channels rather than shadows or broad roads.

questions.question: Does a bare-looking field contain diffuse darker areas?
questions.definition: Require gradual darkening across patches at least 30 metres wide within soil-like ground, excluding cloud shadows, terrain shading and clearly vegetated patches.

questions.question: Do darker ground patches cross more than one field?
questions.definition: Require a coherent dark-toned pattern on exposed-looking ground to continue across a visible parcel boundary without following a cast-shadow direction.

questions.question: Are dark ground patches concentrated along field margins?
questions.definition: Require non-shadowed, weakly vegetated dark ground along at least 100 metres of a field edge while most of that field's interior is visibly lighter.

questions.question: Are dark ground patches concentrated inside fields rather than along their edges?
questions.definition: Require at least two non-shadowed dark patches approximately 20 metres across that are enclosed by lighter soil-like ground within field interiors.

questions.question: Does exposed-looking ground grade from dark to pale within one parcel?
questions.definition: Require a broad tonal gradient across at least 100 metres of a largely non-vegetated parcel, excluding obvious illumination effects.

questions.question: Do dark open-ground patches have irregular, lobed outlines?
questions.definition: Require at least two non-shadowed dark patches with curved protrusions or indentations rather than straight parcel-shaped outlines.

questions.question: Do wet-looking dark areas alternate with visibly vegetated areas?
questions.definition: Require repeated interspersion of smooth, weakly red dark ground and red-toned vegetation across at least 100 metres, treating wetness only as an appearance.

questions.question: Does a winding corridor interrupt otherwise straight field boundaries?
questions.definition: Require a curving dark or vegetated strip to truncate or deflect at least two boundaries in an otherwise angular field pattern.

questions.question: Do branching dark or vegetated strips converge into a broader corridor?
questions.definition: Require at least two narrow strips to visibly join a wider continuous strip, without inferring water flow direction or drainage function.

questions.question: Are dark smooth surfaces distinguishable from nearby cast shadows?
questions.definition: Require a dark water-like or ground surface with its own coherent boundary and at least one separate shadow visibly attached to a raised feature.

questions.question: Does a dark or vegetated corridor have a visibly uneven width?
questions.definition: Require a continuous corridor at least 200 metres long whose width changes by approximately a factor of two, excluding perspective or image-edge truncation.

questions.question: Do buildings, fields and woody vegetation all occupy substantial parts of the patch?
questions.definition: Require roof-and-road patterns, bounded open parcels and coarse-textured woody cover each to occupy at least approximately 5 percent of the image.

questions.question: Does a road cross both open fields and woody vegetation?
questions.definition: Require the same traceable road to pass through at least 100 metres of field surroundings and at least 100 metres of woody surroundings.

questions.question: Are the fields closest to buildings visually different from more distant fields?
questions.definition: Require at least two fields beside a building group to share a colour or texture contrast with at least two fields farther away, without assigning a cause.

questions.question: Do small fields occur around a building cluster while larger fields lie farther away?
questions.definition: Require at least two near-cluster parcels whose visible areas are each less than half those of at least two more distant parcels.

questions.question: Does woody vegetation separate buildings from fields?
questions.definition: Require a visible woody strip to lie between a building group and open parcels along at least 100 metres of their facing edges.

questions.question: Do vegetation strips connect a built-looking area to a larger woody block?
questions.definition: Require a traceable vegetated connection from within approximately 30 metres of roofs to a coarse-textured vegetation block at least 100 metres across.

questions.question: Are intensely red vegetation patches embedded in a mostly non-vegetated setting?
questions.definition: Require at least two strongly red patches approximately 30 metres across surrounded predominantly by bare-looking ground or built surfaces.

questions.question: Are pale non-vegetated patches embedded in a mostly woody setting?
questions.definition: Require at least two pale, weakly red openings approximately 30 metres across within a landscape whose visible surroundings are predominantly coarse-textured vegetation.

questions.question: Do bare-looking and strongly vegetated fields both touch the same woody block?
questions.definition: Require one soil-like parcel and one strongly red parcel each to share at least 50 metres of boundary with the same connected woody area.

questions.question: Does a road separate fields with contrasting vegetation states?
questions.definition: Require at least 100 metres of road with predominantly strong vegetation redness on one side and pale or weakly vegetated field cover on the other.

questions.question: Do fields beside a woody edge contain visible edge-to-interior colour changes?
questions.definition: Require a colour change extending approximately 20 metres or more into at least one adjoining field, excluding a narrow cast shadow from the woody edge.

questions.question: Does a large open parcel contrast with a finely divided neighbouring landscape?
questions.definition: Require one field covering at least 10 percent of the patch beside an area containing at least five smaller parcels, vegetation strips or building groups.

questions.question: Do both straight and sinuous vegetation corridors occur in the patch?
questions.definition: Require one vegetation strip approximately straight for 150 metres and another that bends conspicuously over a comparable length.

questions.question: Are isolated woody clumps accompanied by continuous woody boundaries?
questions.definition: Require at least two detached coarse-textured vegetation clumps and at least one woody boundary strip extending approximately 150 metres.

questions.question: Does a road interrupt an otherwise connected vegetation strip?
questions.definition: Require aligned vegetation segments on opposite sides of a visible road, with the road forming the principal gap between them.

questions.question: Does a vegetation corridor widen into a larger vegetation patch?
questions.definition: Require a narrow vegetated strip at least 100 metres long to merge continuously into a patch at least three times its width.

questions.question: Do the most irregular field edges occur beside woody vegetation?
questions.definition: Require at least two fields with visibly curved or indented woody-facing edges and comparatively straight edges facing other open parcels.

questions.question: Does a built-looking group occupy a gap between vegetation blocks?
questions.definition: Require roof-like surfaces situated between two substantial vegetation blocks whose facing edges lie within approximately 100 metres of the buildings.

questions.question: Are vegetated and exposed-looking strips aligned in the same direction?
questions.definition: Require at least two vegetation bands and two pale or brown ground bands with approximately parallel long axes across a common open area.

questions.question: Does a winding corridor separate contrasting field patterns?
questions.definition: Require a curving dark or vegetated strip with visibly different parcel size, orientation or colour patterns on its two sides for at least 150 metres.

questions.question: Are dark ground patches associated with stronger nearby vegetation redness?
questions.definition: Require at least two non-shadowed dark ground patches bordered by vegetation that is conspicuously redder than vegetation farther away in the same open area.

questions.question: Does a narrow vegetation strip cross predominantly pale open land?
questions.definition: Require a red-toned strip at least 200 metres long with pale, weakly vegetated ground occupying most of the visible area on both sides.

questions.question: Do fields and roads share a dominant geometric alignment?
questions.definition: Require at least three field boundaries and two road segments to be approximately parallel or perpendicular to the same dominant direction.

questions.question: Does a road cut obliquely across the dominant field alignment?
questions.definition: Require a road at least 200 metres long that intersects the prevailing direction of at least three field boundaries at an angle clearly different from a right angle.

questions.question: Are visibly vegetated openings present inside a larger woody area?
questions.definition: Require at least two smooth-textured, red-toned openings approximately 30 metres across substantially surrounded by coarse-textured woody vegetation.

questions.question: Do neighbouring open areas differ in both colour and internal texture?
questions.definition: Require two adjoining open areas with a clear colour contrast and a separate texture contrast, such as uniform versus banded or smooth versus mottled.

questions.question: Are buildings concentrated where several open parcels meet?
questions.definition: Require a roof-like cluster within approximately 50 metres of the convergence of at least three distinguishable field or open-ground parcels.

questions.question: Does vegetation form a partial ring around a contrasting open or built area?
questions.definition: Require a connected vegetated belt surrounding at least three quarters of an area at least 50 metres across while leaving a visible opening.

questions.question: Do narrow woody strips and broad woody blocks show different false-colour tones?
questions.definition: Require a woody strip and a woody block in the same patch to differ consistently in redness over non-shadowed portions at least 100 metres long.

questions.question: Does the patch combine a broad uniform area with a heterogeneous margin?
questions.definition: Require a visually uniform cover area occupying at least one quarter of the patch beside a margin containing at least three distinct cover patterns in smaller units.
